candidate.answerReason: A whole-number quotient can be written with the dividend as numerator and the positive divisor as denominator, giving 7/4.

methods.label: Write the quotient as a fraction
methods.explanation: \(7\div4=\frac{7}{4}\). The numerator is greater than the denominator, so it is an improper fraction.
methods.levelReason: Writing whole-number division as a fraction and identifying an improper fraction fit grade 5; no reciprocal or sign rule is used.

needsNewNodes.name: Whole-number division expressed as a fraction
needsNewNodes.description: For a nonnegative whole number \(a\) and a positive whole number \(b\), express \(a\div b\) as \(\frac{a}{b}\). Connect this relationship to equal sharing, identify the dividend as numerator and divisor as denominator, and include quotients greater than 1.
needsNewNodes.reason: This is the decisive relationship in 7 divided by 4. The existing division-meaning and fraction-meaning nodes supply background but do not explicitly cover this grade-5 relationship; cnm_017 instead specifies later reciprocal and sign rules.

limitations: The decisive quotient-to-fraction relationship lacks a precise grade-5 catalog ID.
candidate.changeReason: 7 divided by 4 equals 7/4, and 7 greater than 4 correctly identifies an improper fraction. The existing explanation is mathematically correct and sufficient; the annotation gap does not require a prose revision.
